question: A weekly digest produced with help from a project turns out to have been based on a source that has since been found unreliable. What should the person who publishes the digest do?
options: A) Tell the recipients which past digests are affected and correct the source before the next one.
B) Add a standing disclaimer to all future digests saying that any figure in them may be inaccurate.
C) Stop producing the digest, since a source problem means the workflow can never be trusted again.
D) Quietly swap the source and let the correction show up in future digests without further comment.
correct_answers: A) Tell the recipients which past digests are affected and correct the source before the next one.
explanations: Correct. Maintenance includes informing the people who already acted on the earlier output.
A permanent disclaimer neither corrects the past nor restores confidence in the future.
One bad source is a maintenance failure, not a reason to abandon a working process.
Recipients keep relying on earlier digests they have no reason to doubt.
